items.followUp: Define a scientific theory and give one example.

rubric.why: A scientific law describes a consistently observed natural phenomenon.
rubric.description: Defines a scientific law as a statement describing a consistently observed natural phenomenon.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the idea that a law describes a repeatedly observed phenomenon or relationship.

rubric.why: Examples show understanding of the kinds of statements that may be scientific laws.
rubric.description: Gives two valid examples of scientific laws.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid examples.

modelAnswer: A scientific law is a statement that describes a natural phenomenon or relationship consistently observed through repeated observations.
Examples include the law of gravitation and the law of conservation of energy.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a threatened species and an extinct species.

rubric.why: Extinction means that no living individuals of the species remain.
rubric.description: States that an extinct species has no living members.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for clearly stating that no individuals of the species remain alive.

rubric.why: An endangered species still exists but faces a serious risk of extinction.
rubric.description: States that an endangered species is still living but is at risk of extinction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for distinguishing endangered species as existing species threatened with extinction.

modelAnswer: An extinct species has no living members remaining.
An endangered species still has living members but is at risk of extinction.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the net movement of particles down their concentration gradient.
rubric.description: Defines diffusion as movement of particles from higher to lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the direction of movement and the term particles or molecules.

rubric.why: Osmosis specifically involves water moving across a selectively permeable membrane.
rubric.description: Distinguishes osmosis as movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying water and the membrane.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
Osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution.

items.followUp: Explain how materials enter a cell by endocytosis and leave it by exocytosis.

rubric.why: Endocytosis brings material into the cell by enclosing it in a membrane-bound vesicle.
rubric.description: Explains that endocytosis takes material into the cell in a vesicle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for inward movement and vesicle formation or membrane engulfment.

rubric.why: Exocytosis releases material when a vesicle fuses with the cell membrane.
rubric.description: Explains that exocytosis releases material from the cell by vesicle fusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for outward release and vesicle fusion or equivalent.

modelAnswer: Endocytosis is the uptake of material into a cell when the cell membrane engulfs it and forms a vesicle.
Exocytosis is the release of material from a cell when a vesicle fuses with the cell membrane.

items.followUp: Name the two major phases of the cell cycle and state what happens in each.

rubric.why: The cell cycle is the sequence of events between successive cell divisions.
rubric.description: Defines the cell cycle as the events from one cell division to the next.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear definition involving the sequence or interval between divisions.

rubric.why: Interphase and the mitotic phase are the major phases of the cell cycle.
rubric.description: Names interphase and the mitotic phase as its major phases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both phases.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the sequence of events through which a cell passes from one division to the next.
Its major phases are interphase and the mitotic phase (M phase).

items.followUp: What is a phragmoplast, and how does it help in cytokinesis in plant cells?

rubric.why: The term in the question appears to refer to the phragmoplast, a microtubule structure involved in plant-cell cytokinesis.
rubric.description: Identifies the phagoplasm/phragmoplast as a structure associated with plant-cell division, particularly the cell plate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the structure as the phragmoplast or associating it with microtubules and the cell plate.

rubric.why: The phragmoplast helps organize cell-plate formation between the daughter nuclei.
rubric.description: States that it helps form or guide the cell plate, which separates the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the role in cell-plate formation or separation of the daughter cells.

modelAnswer: “Phagoplasm” in this question appears to refer to the phragmoplast, a structure of microtubules formed during plant-cell division.
It guides the formation of the cell plate between the daughter nuclei; the cell plate develops into a new cell wall separating the daughter cells.

items.followUp: Differentiate between benign and malignant tumors.

rubric.why: Benign tumors remain localized and do not spread to other parts of the body.
rubric.description: States that benign tumors are localized and do not spread.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a benign tumor as non-invasive or not spreading.

rubric.why: Malignant tumors invade tissues and can spread to other parts of the body.
rubric.description: States that malignant tumors invade or spread to other parts of the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying invasion, spread, or metastasis.

modelAnswer: Benign tumors are usually localized and do not invade or spread to other parts of the body.
Malignant tumors are cancerous; they invade surrounding tissues and may spread to other parts of the body (metastasis).

items.followUp: Differentiate between anabolic and catabolic reactions, including their energy changes.

rubric.why: Catabolism breaks complex molecules into simpler ones.
rubric.description: Defines catabolism as the breakdown of complex molecules into simpler molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the breakdown direction.
Award 1 mark for the energy change.

rubric.why: Anabolism builds complex molecules from simpler ones.
rubric.description: Defines anabolism as synthesis of complex molecules from simpler molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the synthesis direction.

rubric.description: States that anabolism uses or requires energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the energy change.

modelAnswer: Catabolism is the breakdown of complex molecules into simpler molecules, releasing energy.
Anabolism is the synthesis of complex molecules from simpler molecules, requiring energy.
